theCorrection.rule: A reservation may be released by the attempt that is refusing it before any dispatch is possible. That attempt knows nothing was sent, so the installation's answered-record adds nothing there.
theCorrection.whatItDoesNotChange: The cross-attempt rule is untouched. A RETRY of an unresolved reservation is still permitted only when the installation's record positively says the question went unanswered; answered refuses, unknown refuses.
theCorrection.whatItWillNeverDo: It never touches an entry carrying recorded usage. A call that happened is not this function's to erase, in any circumstance.
theCorrection.residualStated: If a project were de-authorised AFTER a real call was dispatched but before its settlement landed, this would release that reservation and the month would lose an estimate for spend that may really have occurred. It costs an estimate rather than a governance decision, and the alternative — a phantom charge that can never be cleared and a question that can never be asked again — is what actually blocked this witness twice.
theCorrection.alsoFixed: A rehearsal (`--dry-run`) reserved its estimate and never released it, so the next real attempt refused it as unaskable. That is how the first one-call authorisation was lost. The rehearsal now releases what it reserved.
